title: Requirements to teach English in Vietnam (2026)
description: Degree plus 2 years' experience for the work permit, what a TEFL really does, and 2026 answers for non-native speakers, over-50s and no-degree teachers.
h1: Requirements to teach English in Vietnam: the law, what employers ask, and the hard cases
intro: To teach English legally in Vietnam you need a work permit, which for teachers means a bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years of relevant experience (Decree 219/2025), a police check issued within 6 months of filing and a health check in Vietnam. Language centres must also see a suitable teaching certificate; employers usually want a 120-hour TEFL, TESOL or CELTA. The law sets no maximum age, and non-native speakers are not barred, though language centres may need C1-level English proof from them.
keyPoints: The work permit is the real gate: teachers are filed as **experts**, which means a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant experience under Decree 219/2025 (in force since 7 August 2025; the old rule was 3 years).

A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience. It is the education-side requirement for language centres, and the law sets no minimum hours: **120 hours is an employer convention**.

Your police check must be issued no more than 6 months before the employer files, the health check is done in Vietnam, and since 11 September 2026 an apostille replaces embassy legalisation for documents from Convention countries (not Germany, Austria or Czechia, which objected, nor Thailand until 28 February 2027).
There is no established legal route for teachers without a degree. Working without a permit costs the teacher {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and possibly deportation under Decree 283/2026.

Non-native speakers are not barred by law: at language centres they need Level 5 (about C1) English proof unless their degree is in English or English teaching, and a teaching certificate unless the degree is in English teaching.
Neither the Labour Code nor Decree 219 sets a maximum age. Age bands in job ads are employer preferences, not law.

sections.title: Requirements for foreign teachers at a glance: the law vs what employers ask

blocks.text: Two sets of rules apply, and employers add a third layer. The work permit, governed by [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) since 7 August 2025, decides whether you may work at all; it replaced the foreign-worker rules of Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. Teachers are filed as **experts**: a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant work experience (Art 3(3)(a)).

The education rules set the teaching standard on top. For language centres that is MOET's [Circular 21/2018/TT-BGDĐT](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-21-2018-tt-bgddt-quy-che-to-chuc-hoat-dong-cua-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-166595-d1.html), which Decree 219 Art 19(3)(đ) pulls into the permit file. Then each employer adds its own preferences.

blocks.text: In Ho Chi Minh City the permit is issued by the Department of Home Affairs (Sở Nội vụ) for employers outside export-processing zones, industrial parks and high-tech parks, which covers practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html), 21 September 2026). The employer applies, not you: it files 60 to 10 days before your start date, the decree allows up to 10 working days for a decision and the city publishes 5, and the {{vnd:600000}} state fee is the employer's to pay.

The whole procedure is in [our guide to the work permit for English teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers). This page explains the rules; on any individual file, your employer and the authority have the final word.

sections.title: Your degree: does the subject matter, and how to get it accepted

blocks.text: For the work permit, Decree 219 asks for a bachelor's degree or higher, or equivalent, and names no subject. What has to fit the job is your **experience**, which must be 'suited to the job position'. For a native speaker at a language centre, Circular 21/2018 Art 18(5) asks for less: a college degree in any field. In practice the bachelor's needed for the permit is the binding requirement.

It has to be a real degree. A course-completion certificate, a TEFL included, is not equivalent to a university degree ([LuatVietnam](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-thue-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-can-dieu-kien-gi-883-100926-article.html)). Employers can ask for more than the law: [ILA's job pages](https://teachingenglish.ila.edu.vn/job-detail/?id=1) want a bachelor's of at least three years, and international schools look for a teaching degree or licence as well.
Getting the degree accepted: apostille, translation, certification

Foreign documents in a work-permit file must be legalised, or exempt under a treaty, then translated into Vietnamese and certified; a copy must be certified against the original before it is translated (Decree 219 Art 5). Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from 11 September 2026 under [Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/293_2026_nd-cp_23072026_1-signed.signed.pdf), so a degree from a member country needs one apostille from the issuing country instead of embassy legalisation.

items: **Apostille works** for the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa and the Philippines, none of which objected ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)).

**Still legalisation**: Germany, Austria and Czechia objected to Vietnam's accession ([HCCH notifications](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/notifications/?csid=1557&disp=type)), so their documents still go through consular legalisation. Thai documents do too until the Convention takes effect for Thailand on 28 February 2027.

**Translation is still needed**: an apostille never replaces it. Since 1 July 2025 a translation is made valid by certifying the translator's signature at a ward People's Committee or a notary office ([Nhân Dân](https://nhandan.vn/nhieu-quy-dinh-moi-ve-cong-chung-post892108.html)).
**Legalised before 11 September 2026?** Those documents stay valid; you do not need to redo them as apostilles.

blocks.text: Ministry of Education recognition of your foreign degree is not on the Decree 219 dossier list; the authority checks the apostilled or legalised degree and its certified translation. Country-by-country steps, costs and the trap with private certificates (a TEFL from a private provider usually needs a notary or solicitor first) are in [getting your degree and documents authenticated](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam).

sections.title: Teaching certificate: what counts as a 'suitable' TEFL, TESOL or CELTA

blocks.text: A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience in the work-permit test. It is the education-side requirement: Circular 21/2018 asks foreign teachers at language centres for a 'suitable' foreign-language teaching certificate. No Vietnamese text sets a minimum number of hours, so **'120 hours' is an employer convention**, not law.

In December 2020 MOET wrote to Hanoi's labour department recommending that TESOL, TEFL and CELTA certificates be accepted for work permits, citing courses from named accredited awarding bodies ([Giáo dục Việt Nam](https://giaoduc.net.vn/bo-giao-duc-go-roi-quy-dinh-cap-phep-cho-giao-vien-tieng-anh-nuoc-ngoai-post214387.gd)). Accreditation matters: in January 2026 HCMC's education department reviewed foreign teachers in public-school linked programmes and flagged those holding only completion certificates instead of the required teaching certificate ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html)).

blocks.text: One official option is little known: MOET [Decision 4159/QĐ-BGDĐT](https://lsvn.vn/nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-day-tieng-anh-tai-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-se-duoc-cap-chung-chi-dao-tao-1709006169-a141314.html) (6 December 2023) created a 160-period course, 10 modules plus a practicum, and a certificate for foreigners who teach English at language centres without a teaching qualification. Universities with English teacher-training faculties run it; check that your target employer accepts it before you enrol.

Choosing between an online TEFL, an in-class course and CELTA (Apollo IH runs CELTA in the city at {{vnd:42000000}}, or {{vnd:39500000}} if paid 6 weeks ahead) is covered in [TEFL, TESOL or CELTA for Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam).

sections.title: Criminal record check and health check

blocks.text: Labour Code Art 151 requires a foreign worker to meet health standards and to have no current sentence, unexpunged conviction or pending prosecution. Decree 219 turns that into two documents, and the order you get them in matters.

items.title: Order the police check at the right time
items.text: It must be issued no more than 6 months before your employer files, and the employer files 60 to 10 days before your start date. It can come from your home country or from Vietnam. Use your national check: for example, an FBI check is apostilled by the US State Department, not by a state office.

items.title: Apostille first, then translate
items.text: Get the apostille (or legalisation) in the issuing country before the Vietnamese translation, so the translation covers the apostille page too. Then have the translator's signature certified in Vietnam.

items.title: Already living in Vietnam? A Vietnamese record also works
items.text: Since 1 March 2025 Vietnamese criminal records come from the police, not the Department of Justice. In Ho Chi Minh City the counters are at 161 Nguyễn Du (Bến Thành ward), 681 Cách Mạng Tháng 8 (Thủ Dầu Một ward) and 4 Nguyễn Tất Thành (Bà Rịa ward) ([Tuổi Trẻ](https://tuoitre.vn/cong-an-tp-hcm-thay-doi-dia-diem-tiep-nhan-va-tra-ket-qua-ly-lich-tu-phap-20260213171448319.htm)); official addresses have used the new ward names since July 2025, not districts. With your authorisation, the employer can also request it online together with the work permit.

items.title: Do the health check in Vietnam
items.text: A health certificate from abroad is accepted only where Vietnam has a mutual-recognition agreement with that country, so in practice the check is done after you arrive, at a facility qualified in Vietnam ([Government news portal](https://baochinhphu.vn/quy-dinh-moi-ve-cap-giay-phep-cho-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-102250807172724025.htm)). Ask your employer which hospital the authority accepts. A draft amendment that would accept certificates from abroad was not in force as of October 2026.

blocks.title: The six-month clock
blocks.text: The 6 months run from the date your police check is **issued** to the date the employer files, not to your start date and not from the apostille date. Courier, apostille and translation time all eat into the window, and an out-of-date check gets the file rejected. Time the order backwards from the filing date.
Country routes (FBI, ACRO or DBS, RCMP, AFP and others) are in [our criminal record check guide](/teach-in-vietnam/criminal-record-check-for-a-vietnam-work-permit).

sections.title: Can you teach English in Vietnam without a degree?

blocks.text: Not legally, on the route teachers use. The expert category needs a bachelor's degree or higher, and [Decree 219](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) removed the old route that let people qualify as experts without a degree after 5 years in the field. A TEFL or CELTA does not stand in for the degree, and a college or associate degree, enough under Circular 21 at a language centre, does not meet the expert test.

Decree 219 also has a 'technical worker' category (at least 1 year of training plus 2 years' relevant experience, or 3 years' experience). Teachers rarely use it, and whether Ho Chi Minh City would issue a teaching permit on that basis to someone without a bachelor's is untested, so do not plan a move around it. The under-90-days-a-year exemption is not a way round either: it covers people who already qualify as experts, managers or technical workers, and the employer must still notify the authority.
What teaching without a permit risks

blocks.caption: Fines for working without a work permit under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, in force since 10 September 2026.
rows: Doubled for an organisation such as a company, school or centre

blocks.text: The amounts are set by [Decree 283/2026](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-283-2026-nd-cp-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-lao-dong-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-440485-d1.html). There is a quieter cost too. Experience gained in Vietnam counts toward the 2-year expert test only through a previous Vietnamese work permit, so years taught without one cannot be proved later.

Enforcement is real. In April 2026 officials in Thanh Hoa found foreign teachers working at kindergartens their permits did not name, and said that teaching, substituting, trial lessons or observing classes without a permit is illegal ([Báo Thanh Hóa](https://baothanhhoa.vn/vi-pham-trong-su-dung-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-tai-co-so-mam-non-283585.htm)). In Ho Chi Minh City, the education department told centres in January 2024 to show each foreign teacher's work permit before that teacher starts in a school ([VOH](https://voh.com.vn/giao-duc/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tai-tphcm-khong-duoc-thu-hoc-phi-dai-han-510985.html)), and since January 2026 it has required a work permit and certified degrees in the file of every foreign teacher in public-school linked programmes ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html)). Old forum claims that 'nobody checks' are out of date, and packages selling 'TEFL plus a guaranteed job' to people without degrees do not change the law.

sections.title: Non-native English speakers: the legal position and what employers do

blocks.text: Decree 219 sets no native-speaker or nationality condition for a work permit ([Decree 219 text](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html)); the degree and the 2 years' experience apply to everyone. The education rule does distinguish. MOET has read 'native speaker' as someone whose first language is the language taught, and everyone else teaching at a language centre must meet one of three routes in Circular 21/2018 Art 18(6).

blocks.caption: The three routes for non-native teachers at language centres under Circular 21/2018 Art 18(6). The work permit's bachelor's degree and 2 years' experience apply on top.
rows: College degree or higher in foreign-language teacher training
College degree or higher in English
College degree or higher in any field
Level 5 English proof (about CEFR C1) and a suitable teaching certificate

blocks.text: Proving Level 5 (about C1)

Vietnam's 6-level framework maps onto the CEFR, so Level 5 is about C1. No MOET-wide table converts a test score to Level 5; institutions set their own, and Hanoi University of Science and Technology's 2023 list puts Level 5 at IELTS 7.0 to 8.0 ([HUST](https://hust.edu.vn/uploads/sys/su-kien-noi-bat/2023_08/qd7806.2023-ban-hanh-danh-muc-quy-doi-tuong-duong-cac-chung-chi-tieng-anh.pdf)). IELTS 7.0 or above is the common working benchmark, and recruiters often cite 6.5 to 7.0+, but those numbers are employer and agency practice, not law.

Use an internationally recognised test such as IELTS, TOEFL or a Cambridge exam. In May 2026 police broke up a scheme selling unauthorised 'CEFR-equivalent' English certificates and asked organisations to review any they had accepted ([Viet Nam News](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1780870/viet-nam-busts-fake-english-certification-scam-worth-nearly-8-million.html)).
What employers actually do

Employers are stricter than the law. ILA lists 'Native' English as a requirement, and some recruiters ask for passports from English-speaking countries. Others hire non-native speakers with strong English: [VUS](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979) says it considers non-native applicants who send an intro video. CELTA itself does not require native-speaker status, though International House asks candidates for C1 or above ([IH](https://ihteachenglish.com/?p=13232)). How bias shows up in ads and pay, and how to work around it, is in [hiring bias in teaching jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/discrimination-and-hiring-bias-in-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Over 50 or 55: age limits in the rules and in practice

blocks.text: There is no upper age limit in the law. Labour Code Art 151 sets a minimum of 18, and neither the Labour Code nor Decree 219 sets a maximum for a work permit ([Decree 219 text](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html)). Any upper limit you meet comes from employer or insurer practice. Some ads set age bands, such as a 2026 Ho Chi Minh City kindergarten ad asking for teachers aged 23 to 40, but that is a preference, not a legal condition.
Health is the legal test at every age: you need the work-permit health certificate described above, done in Vietnam. Two money points change with age.

items: **Social insurance**: foreign employees on contracts of 12 months or more must join compulsory social insurance (employee 9.5%, of which 8% pension and 1.5% health insurance; employer 20.5%). Vietnam's statutory retirement age in 2026 is 61 years 6 months for men and 57 for women, and anyone who had already reached it when signing the contract is exempt ([Social Insurance Law 2024, Art 2(2)](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/law-41-2024-qh15-on-social-insurance-360809-d1.html)), so ask the employer how your payslip and health cover will work.

**Health cover**: ask exactly what health insurance comes with the job (some chains, such as [Apollo English](https://www.theteflacademy.com/?p=61627), advertise comprehensive health insurance) and read any age terms in the policy before you sign.

blocks.text: A long working history can make the 2-year experience test easier to document, provided your letters show experience the authority accepts as relevant to the job. Hospitals, costs and insurance options are in [healthcare and health insurance in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/healthcare-and-health-insurance-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: No teaching experience: how first-timers get hired

blocks.text: There are two separate questions: will an employer take you, and will the permit file go through. On the employer side, the big chains do hire first-timers. ILA calls teaching practice 'highly preferred', not mandatory, for most locations (it makes 3 years' English-teaching experience compulsory for Da Nang, Nha Trang and Vung Tau). VUS welcomes newly certified teachers, says most new expat teachers start at {{vnd:450000}} an hour gross, and offers its 12-month contract after a probation month and once the work permit is issued. Probation is paid work, so confirm the permit is issued before that month begins: teaching without one costs {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and possible deportation.
The permit side: the 2-year rule

The expert test asks for 2 years of relevant experience. The usual proof is a letter from a past employer **abroad** stating your years of experience; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits. For experts in education, Decree 219 Art 19(3) also lists, as an alternative proof, documents showing you meet the qualification standard set by education law (point đ). How Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is not published.

So if you have less than 2 years' experience, **ask the employer which proof they will file for you, and get the answer in writing before you travel**. Whether TEFL or CELTA teaching practice counts as experience has not been confirmed either. Never use an experience letter that is not true: an employer that files altered or forged documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-60000000}} ({{vnd:80000000-120000000}} for a company, school or centre) under Decree 283/2026, and a permit issued in breach of the rules can be revoked.
What gets first-timers hired

items: **A course with real teaching practice.** In Ho Chi Minh City, TEFL International Vietnam, Ninja Teacher Academy and AVSE TESOL run in-class courses with live practice, and ILA names Ninja and AVSE as acceptable; CELTA is the other route.

**Experience letters for anything relevant you did abroad**: on letterhead, with your job title, exact start and end dates, a signature and contact details. A reference letter is a private document, so it usually needs a notary or solicitor's certification before the apostille or legalisation.

**A prepared demo lesson.** Ask who will watch, the learners' age and level and how long it should run; see [the CV, interview and demo lesson guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-cv-and-demo-lesson-in-vietnam).

**Postings you can trace.** eno.vn's [teaching jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) links postings to the original ad where there is one, and you apply there; the [school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers with teachers' reviews where there are any. Never pay to get a job.

**Realistic targets.** International schools are the exception: [SSIS](https://search.openapply.com/schools/saigon-south-international-school), for example, normally hires teachers with a master's, at least 2 years' experience and home-country certification. See [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).

faqs.q: Is there an age limit to teach English in Vietnam?
faqs.a: There is no upper age limit in the law: Labour Code Art 151 sets a minimum age of 18, and neither the Labour Code nor Decree 219 sets a maximum for a work permit. Any upper limit you meet comes from employers or insurers, such as a 2026 Ho Chi Minh City kindergarten ad asking for teachers aged 23 to 40; at every age, the legal test is the work-permit health check, which in practice is done in Vietnam.

faqs.q: Can I teach without IELTS or a native passport?
faqs.a: No law requires IELTS or a particular passport: Decree 219 sets no nationality or native-speaker condition for the work permit. At a language centre, a teacher whose first language is not English needs Level 5 (about C1) English proof, such as an IELTS, TOEFL or Cambridge result, unless their degree is in English or English teaching, and a teaching certificate unless it is in English teaching. Employers can be stricter: ILA lists 'Native' English as a requirement, while VUS says it considers non-native applicants who send an intro video.

faqs.q: Do I need my degree recognised by Vietnam's Ministry of Education for the work permit?
faqs.a: No. Ministry of Education recognition is not on the Decree 219 dossier list. The authority checks your degree with an apostille (or legalisation) and a certified Vietnamese translation.

faqs.q: Is a 100-hour TEFL enough to teach in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The law sets no minimum hours; it asks only for a suitable teaching certificate. Many employers set 120 hours as their floor, ILA among them, so check the posting before you buy a course.

faqs.q: Do I need a Vietnamese police check as well as one from home?
faqs.a: No. Decree 219 accepts either a home-country or a Vietnamese criminal record, as long as it was issued no more than 6 months before filing. The law sets no minimum stay before a foreigner who has lived in Vietnam can request a Vietnamese one.

faqs.q: My documents were legalised by a Vietnamese embassy before September 2026. Do I need to redo them?
faqs.a: No. Documents legalised before 11 September 2026 remain valid under Decree 293/2026, and offices may not ask you to replace them with an apostille. You still need a certified Vietnamese translation.

faqs.q: Does a job in Binh Duong or Vung Tau count as Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 1 July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City includes the former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces, so a school there files with the Ho Chi Minh City authorities.

faqs.q: Can I start teaching while my work permit is being processed?
faqs.a: No. Teaching before the permit is issued is working without a permit, which since 10 September 2026 carries a fine for you and possible deportation, plus a fine for the employer. Wait for the permit and the signed labour contract.
